precedence.rationale: OpenCode v2.3.2 precedence between the two active global files (opencode.json, opencode.jsonc) and a project override is undocumented in available material. Read-only inspection cannot prove a runtime winner; both mapping surfaces reference byte-identical templates, so observed output could not distinguish them either.
precedence.evidence_gap: Proving precedence requires command discovery in an isolated sandbox (ASM-01), which is runtime activity outside M1 scope.

steps: Create sandbox <temp>/opencode/m2-probe with home/ and project/; never touch the real $HOME.
Config A (project only): project/.opencode/opencode.json maps e2e to sentinel-A; no global config.
Config B (global json only): home/.config/opencode/opencode.json maps e2e to sentinel-B; no project config.
Config C (dual global): both home configs declare e2e with distinct sentinels; no project config.
Config D (all three): project + both globals, each sentinel distinct.
For each config, invoke /e2e help with HOME redirected into the sandbox and record which sentinel the output echoes.
Record the winner per config, or INCONCLUSIVE with the observed output. Never assume the project wins.
Delete the sandbox by literal path and re-hash the real global configs against SOURCE-BASELINE-FROZEN.md.
probe.cleanup: Delete the sandbox tree with a literal-path delete, then verify the real $HOME config hashes are unchanged.
guardrails: no config writes outside the sandbox
